sender.en: A buyer on OLX or Facebook Marketplace, often claiming to be in the army

name.en: Fake buyer sends a QR code “to pay you”

how.en: You list something for sale online. A buyer, often claiming to be an army officer being transferred and sending an ID card, agrees to your price at once. To “pay” or “verify your account” he sends a QR code or payment request; when you scan it and enter your UPI PIN, money leaves your account. He blames a technical glitch and sends more codes “to refund”. You never need to scan a QR code or enter your UPI PIN to receive money.

text.en: A buyer agrees quickly, sometimes saying he is an army officer and sending an ID.
He sends a QR code or payment request so you can “receive” the money.
You are asked to enter your UPI PIN to get paid.
After money goes, he sends more codes to “refund” it.

Sir I am in Army, posted at Pathankot, I will take the sofa at your price. Our payments go through the army account so I am sending a QR code, scan and enter PIN to receive ₹1 first for verification, then I will send full amount.

en: buyer sent qr code to pay me
scan qr code to receive money
enter upi pin to receive payment
buyer said technical glitch and sent another qr
olx buyer verification of one rupee
Scanning a QR code or entering a UPI PIN to receive money.
A buyer who doesn't haggle and won't meet.
“Army” IDs, transfer stories and canteen cards.
Never scan a buyer's QR code or enter your PIN to get paid.
Ask buyers to pay by entering your UPI ID themselves, or meet in person.
If money went, call 1930 and your bank right away.
